questions.questionText: A rectangular solid is standing on a base of area 48 square metre. Its height is 3 metre and diagonal is 13 metre.

parts.text: The lengths of two sides of a triangle are 19 cm and 20 cm respectively and the angle included between them is \\\(45^\circ \\\), determine the area of the triangle.
parts.answer:
Area of the triangle = \\\(\frac{1}{2} \times 19 \times 20 \times \sin 45^\circ \\\)
[Using the formula for area with two sides and the included angle]
= \\\(190 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\\)
[Simplifying \\\(\frac{1}{2} \times 19 \times 20 \\\) and substituting \\\(\sin 45^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\\)]
= 134.35 sq. cm (approx.) [Ans.]
[Calculating the final numerical value]

parts.text: Determine the length and breadth of the rectangular solid.
parts.answer:
Let length = \( a \) and breadth = \( b \).
[Assigning variables to length and breadth]
Base Area: \( ab = 48 \) --- (i)
[Given the area of the base is 48 sq m]
Given height \( h = 3 \) m and diagonal \( d = 13 \) m.
[Listing the given dimensions]
Length of diagonal \( d^2 = a^2 + b^2 + h^2 \)
[Formula for the diagonal of a rectangular solid]
\( 13^2 = a^2 + b^2 + 3^2 \)
[Substituting the known values]
\( 169 = a^2 + b^2 + 9 \)
[Squaring 13 and 3]
\( a^2 + b^2 = 160 \) --- (ii)
[Subtracting 9 from both sides]
Now, \( (a + b)^2 = a^2 + b^2 + 2ab \)
[Using the algebraic identity for the square of a sum]
\( (a + b)^2 = 160 + 2(48) \)
[Substituting values from (i) and (ii)]
\( (a + b)^2 = 160 + 96 = 256 \)
[Performing the addition]
\\\(a + b = \sqrt{256} = 16 \\\) --- (iii)
[Taking the square root; length and breadth must be positive]
Again, \( (a - b)^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab \)
[Using the algebraic identity for the square of a difference]
\( (a - b)^2 = 160 - 2(48) \)
[Substituting values from (i) and (ii)]
\( (a - b)^2 = 160 - 96 = 64 \)
[Performing the subtraction]
\\\(a - b = \sqrt{64} = 8 \\\) --- (iv)
[Taking the square root; assuming length \( a > b \)]
Adding equations (iii) and (iv):
\( (a + b) + (a - b) = 16 + 8 \)
[Summing the two linear equations]
\( 2a = 24 \)
[Simplifying the left side]
\( a = 12 \) metre
[Dividing by 2]
Substituting \( a = 12 \) in (iii):
\( 12 + b = 16 \)
[Placing the value of \( a \) back into the sum equation]
\( b = 4 \) metre
[Subtracting 12 from both sides]
So, length = 12 m and breadth = 4 m [Ans.]
[Final dimensions determined]

parts.text: An iron pipe of 5 cm is made by taking length and breadth of the rectangular solid as outer and inner diameter respectively. If the weight of each cubic centimetre of iron is 7.2 gm, determine the weight of the rod.
parts.answer:
Outer diameter = Length of solid = 12 m = 1200 cm
[Taking the length as the outer diameter and converting to cm]
Outer radius, \\\(R = \frac{1200}{2} = 600 \\\) cm
[Radius is half of the diameter]
Inner diameter = Breadth of solid = 4 m = 400 cm
[Taking the breadth as the inner diameter and converting to cm]
Inner radius, \\\(r = \frac{400}{2} = 200 \\\) cm
[Radius is half of the diameter]
Height of the pipe, \( h = 5 \) cm
[Given height]
Volume of iron = \\\(\pi(R^2 - r^2)h \\\)
[Formula for the volume of a hollow cylinder]
= \\\(3.1416 \times (600^2 - 200^2) \times 5 \\\)
[Substituting the radius and height values]
= \\\(3.1416 \times (360000 - 40000) \times 5 \\\)
[Squaring the radii]
= \\\(3.1416 \times 320000 \times 5 \\\)
[Calculating the difference]
= 5026560 cubic cm
[Calculating the total volume]
Weight of iron = \\\(5026560 \times 7.2 \\\)
[Multiplying volume by the weight per cubic cm]
= 36191232 gm
[Calculating the product]
= 36191.232 kg [Ans.]
[Converting grams to kilograms by dividing by 1000]

questions.questionText: In the figure, \\\(EF \parallel BD \\\) and \( AC = 16 \) metre.

parts.text: Determine the value of \\\(\csc \angle ABC\\\).
parts.answer:
Since \\\(EF \parallel BD \\\), \\\(\angle ABC = \angle EAB \\\)
[Alternate interior angles are equal when lines are parallel]
Given \\\(\angle EAB = 60^\circ \\\), so \\\(\angle ABC = 60^\circ \\\)
[Substitute the given value]
Value of \\\(\csc \angle ABC = \csc 60^\circ \\\)
[Looking for the cosecant of the angle]
= \\\(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \\\) [Ans.]
[The value of \\\(\csc 60^\circ \\\) is \\\(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \\\)]

parts.text: Determine the area of \\\(\Delta ABC\\\).
parts.answer:
In the right-angled triangle \\\(\Delta ABC \\\),
[Considering the triangle formed by the height AC and base BC]
\\\(\cot \angle ABC = \frac{BC}{AC} \\\)
[Cotangent is the ratio of adjacent side to opposite side]
\\\(\cot 60^\circ = \frac{BC}{16} \\\)
[Substitute known values: \\\(\angle ABC = 60^\circ \\\) and \( AC = 16 \)]
\\\(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{BC}{16} \\\)
[The value of \\\(\cot 60^\circ \\\) is \\\(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\\)]
\\\(BC = \frac{16}{\sqrt{3}} \\\) metre
[Rearranging to find the length of BC]
Area of \\\(\Delta ABC = \frac{1}{2} \times AC \times BC \\\)
[Formula for the area of a right-angled triangle]
= \\\(\frac{1}{2} \times 16 \times \frac{16}{\sqrt{3}} \\\)
[Substituting the values of AC and BC]
= \\\(\frac{128}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 73.9 \\\) square metre [Ans.]
[Calculating the final numerical value]

parts.text: Determine the perimeter of \\\(\Delta ACD\\\).
parts.answer:
In the right-angled triangle \\\(\Delta ADC \\\),
[Considering the triangle formed by height AC and base CD]
\\\(\cot \angle ADC = \frac{CD}{AC} \\\)
[Cotangent is the ratio of adjacent side to opposite side]
Since \\\(EF \parallel BD \\\), \\\(\angle ADC = \angle DAF = 30^\circ\\\)
[Alternate interior angles are equal]
\\\(\cot 30^\circ = \frac{CD}{16} \\\)
[Substituting the known values]
\\\(\sqrt{3} = \frac{CD}{16} \\\)
[The value of \\\(\cot 30^\circ \\\) is \\\(\sqrt{3} \\\)]
\\\(CD = 16\sqrt{3} \\\) metre
[Solving for CD]
Now, \\\(\sin \angle ADC = \frac{AC}{AD} \\\)
[Sine is the ratio of opposite side to hypotenuse]
\\\(\sin 30^\circ = \frac{16}{AD} \\\)
[Substituting the known values]
\\\(\frac{1}{2} = \frac{16}{AD} \\\)
[The value of \\\(\sin 30^\circ \\\) is \\\(\frac{1}{2} \\\)]
\\\(AD = 16 \times 2 = 32 \\\) metre
[Solving for the hypotenuse AD]
Perimeter of \\\(\Delta ACD = AC + CD + AD \\\)
[The sum of all three sides of the triangle]
= \\\(16 + 16\sqrt{3} + 32 \\\)
[Substituting the lengths of AC, CD, and AD]
= \\\(48 + 16\sqrt{3} \approx 75.71 \\\) metre [Ans.]
[Calculating the final approximate numerical value]

questions.questionText: The perimeter of a rectangle and a rhombus is equal. The length of the rectangle is 1.5 times of its width and its perimeter is 180 cm.

parts.text: Determine the length of the smaller side of the rectangle.
parts.answer:
Let the smaller side (width) of the rectangle be \( x \) cm.
[Defining the width as a variable]
Length of the rectangle = \( 1.5x \) cm
[Length is 1.5 times the width]
Perimeter of the rectangle = \\\(2(\text{length} + \text{width}) = 180 \\\)
[Using the perimeter formula for a rectangle]
\( 2(1.5x + x) = 180 \)
[Substituting the expressions for length and width]
\( 2(2.5x) = 180 \)
[Simplifying the expression inside the bracket]
\( 5x = 180 \)
[Multiplying 2 by 2.5]
\\\(x = \frac{180}{5} = 36 \\\) cm
[Dividing by 5 to find the width]
The length of the smaller side is 36 cm [Ans.]
[Final result for width]

parts.text: If the larger diagonal of the rhombus is 72 cm, determine the length of the other diagonal.
parts.answer:
Perimeter of the rhombus = Perimeter of the rectangle = 180 cm
[Given that the perimeters are equal]
Length of each side of the rhombus = \\\(\frac{180}{4} = 45 \\\) cm
[A rhombus has 4 equal sides]
Larger diagonal, \( BD = 72 \) cm
[Given value]
Since diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, half of the larger diagonal = \\\(\frac{72}{2} = 36 \\\) cm
[The intersection point divides the diagonal into two equal halves]
Let the other diagonal be \( AC \). In right-angled triangle \\\(\Delta AOD \\\) (where O is the center):
\\\(\text{Side}^2 = (\frac{AC}{2})^2 + (\frac{BD}{2})^2 \\\)
[Applying Pythagoras theorem]
\\\(45^2 = (\frac{AC}{2})^2 + 36^2 \\\)
[Substitute known side and half-diagonal length]
\\\(2025 = (\frac{AC}{2})^2 + 1296 \\\)
[Squaring 45 and 36]
\\\((\frac{AC}{2})^2 = 2025 - 1296 = 729 \\\)
[Subtracting 1296 from both sides]
\\\(\frac{AC}{2} = \sqrt{729} = 27 \\\) cm
[Taking the square root]
Other diagonal, \\\(AC = 27 \times 2 = 54 \\\) cm [Ans.]
[Multiplying the half-diagonal by 2]

parts.text: If the length of each of the equal sides of an isosceles triangle is \\\(\frac{3}{4} \\\) times of its base and its perimeter is half of the perimeter of the rectangle, determine the area of the triangle.
parts.answer:
Perimeter of the isosceles triangle = \\\(\frac{1}{2} \times \text{Perimeter of rectangle} \\\)
[Given the perimeter is half of the rectangle's]
= \\\(\frac{1}{2} \times 180 = 90 \\\) cm
[Calculating the value]
Let the base of the triangle be \( b = x \) cm.
[Defining the base as a variable]
The equal sides are \\\(a = \frac{3}{4}x \\\) cm.
[Given that equal sides are 3/4 of the base]
Perimeter = \( a + a + b = 90 \)
[Formula for the perimeter of an isosceles triangle]
\\\(\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{3}{4}x + x = 90 \\\)
[Substituting the expressions for sides and base]
\\\(\frac{6}{4}x + x = 90 \\\)
[Adding the fractions]
\( 1.5x + x = 90 \)
[Converting \( 6/4 \) to decimal]
\( 2.5x = 90 \)
[Simplifying]
\\\(x = \frac{90}{2.5} = 36 \\\) cm
[Solving for x]
Base, \( b = 36 \) cm and equal sides, \\\(a = \frac{3}{4} \times 36 = 27 \\\) cm
[Finding the specific dimensions of the triangle]
Area of isosceles triangle = \\\(\frac{b}{4}\sqrt{4a^2 - b^2} \\\)
[Formula for the area of an isosceles triangle]
= \\\(\frac{36}{4}\sqrt{4(27)^2 - 36^2} \\\)
[Substituting the values of a and b]
= \\\(9\sqrt{4(729) - 1296} \\\)
[Squaring 27 and 36]
= \\\(9\sqrt{2916 - 1296} \\\)
[Multiplying 4 by 729]
= \\\(9\sqrt{1620} \\\)
[Subtracting]
= \\\(9 \times \sqrt{324 \times 5} = 9 \times 18\sqrt{5} = 162\sqrt{5} \approx 362.24 \\\) sq. cm [Ans.]
[Simplifying the square root and calculating the final area]

questions.questionText: (i) The length of two sides of a parallelogram are 36 cm and 28 cm. Its smaller diagonal is 32 cm. (ii) The area of an equilateral triangle increases by \\\(30\sqrt{3} \\\) sq. metre when the length of each side increases by 4 metre.

parts.text: If the length of each side of a regular pentagon is 8 cm, determine its area.
parts.answer:
Length of each side, \( a = 8 \) cm
[Given value]
Number of sides for a pentagon, \( n = 5 \)
[A pentagon has 5 sides]
Area of a regular pentagon = \\\(\frac{na^2}{4}\cot(\frac{180^\circ}{n}) \\\)
[General formula for the area of a regular polygon]
= \\\(\frac{5 \times 8^2}{4} \cot(\frac{180^\circ}{5}) \\\)
[Substituting the known values]
= \\\(\frac{5 \times 64}{4} \cot(36^\circ) \\\)
[Squaring 8 and dividing by 4]
= \\\(80 \times 0.7265 \approx 110.11 \\\) sq. cm [Ans.]
[Substituting the value of \\\(\cot 36^\circ \\\) and calculating]

parts.text: From stem (ii), find the area of the equilateral triangle.
parts.answer:
Let the original side of the equilateral triangle be \( a \) metre.
[Defining the variable for the side]
Original Area = \\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2 \\\)
[Standard area formula]
New side = \( (a + 4) \) metre
[Side increases by 4 metres]
New Area = \\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(a + 4)^2 \\\)
[Area with the increased side]
According to the question:
\\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(a + 4)^2 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2 = 30\sqrt{3} \\\)
[The difference in areas is \\\(30\sqrt{3} \\\)]
\\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} [ (a + 4)^2 - a^2 ] = 30\sqrt{3} \\\)
[Factoring out \\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \\\)]
\\\((a + 4)^2 - a^2 = 30\sqrt{3} \times \frac{4}{\sqrt{3}} \\\)
[Multiplying both sides by \\\(\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}} \\\)]
\( a^2 + 8a + 16 - a^2 = 120 \)
[Expanding the bracket and simplifying]
\( 8a + 16 = 120 \)
[Subtracting \( a^2 \)]
\( 8a = 104 \)
[Subtracting 16 from both sides]
\\\(a = \frac{104}{8} = 13 \\\) metre
[Solving for the original side length]
Area of the equilateral triangle = \\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 13^2 \\\)
[Substituting the side length back into the formula]
= \\\(\frac{169\sqrt{3}}{4} \\\) sq. m [Ans.]
[Calculating the final value]

parts.text: From stem (i), find the length of the other diagonal of the parallelogram.
parts.answer:
In a parallelogram, the sum of the squares of the four sides is equal to the sum of the squares of the two diagonals.
[Using the parallelogram law]
Let the sides be \( a = 36 \) cm and \( b = 28 \) cm, and diagonals be \( d_1 = 32 \) cm and \( d_2 \).
[Identifying the given values]
\( 2(a^2 + b^2) = d_1^2 + d_2^2 \)
[Writing the parallelogram formula]
\( 2(36^2 + 28^2) = 32^2 + d_2^2 \)
[Substituting the given values]
\( 2(1296 + 784) = 1024 + d_2^2 \)
[Squaring the numbers]
\( 2(2080) = 1024 + d_2^2 \)
[Adding the squares]
\( 4160 = 1024 + d_2^2 \)
[Multiplying by 2]
\( d_2^2 = 4160 - 1024 \)
[Subtracting 1024 from both sides]
\( d_2^2 = 3136 \)
[Calculating the difference]
\\\(d_2 = \sqrt{3136} = 56 \\\) cm [Ans.]
[Taking the square root to find the length of the other diagonal]

questions.questionText: (i) If the length of each side of an equilateral triangle decreases by 1 metre, its area also decreases by \\\(\sqrt{3}\\\) sq. metre. (ii) The area of a rhombus is 1944 sq. cm. and the length of its larger diagonal is 72 cm.

parts.text: Angle subtended by a circular segment at the centre is \\\(60^\circ\\\). If the diameter of the circle is 110 cm., determine the length of the arc.
parts.answer:
Given, diameter of the circle \(= 110\) cm
[Identify the given diameter]
Radius, \\\(r = \frac{110}{2} = 55\\\) cm
[Divide diameter by 2 to find the radius]
Given, central angle \\\(\theta = 60^\circ\\\)
[Identify the given angle]
Length of the arc, \\\(s = \frac{\theta \times \pi \times r}{180}\\\)
[Use the formula for arc length]
\\\(s = \frac{60 \times 3.1416 \times 55}{180}\\\)
[Substitute the values into the formula]
\\\(s \approx 57.6\\\) cm [Ans.]
[Calculate the final value]

parts.text: Determine the length of each side of the equilateral triangle.
parts.answer:
Let the length of each side of the equilateral triangle \(= a\) metre
[Assume the initial side length as a]
Initial area \\\(= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2\\\) square metre
[Use the formula for the area of an equilateral triangle]
If the side decreases by 1 metre, the new side \(= (a - 1)\) metre
[Calculate the new side length]
New area \\\(= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(a - 1)^2\\\) square metre
[Calculate area with the new side length]
According to the question:
\\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(a - 1)^2 = \sqrt{3}\\\)
[Set up the equation based on the decrease in area]
Divide both sides by \\\(\sqrt{3}\\\):
\\\(\frac{1}{4}a^2 - \frac{1}{4}(a - 1)^2 = 1\\\)
[Simplify the equation by removing \\\(\sqrt{3}\\\)]
\\\(\frac{1}{4}[a^2 - (a^2 - 2a + 1)] = 1\\\)
[Expand the square term \((a-1)^2\)]
\\\(\frac{1}{4}(2a - 1) = 1\\\)
[Simplify the terms inside the bracket]
\(2a - 1 = 4\)
[Multiply both sides by 4 to remove the fraction]
\(2a = 5\)
[Add 1 to both sides]
\(a = 2.5\) metre [Ans.]
[Divide by 2 to find the side length]

parts.text: Determine the perimeter of the rhombus.
parts.answer:
Area of the rhombus \(= 1944\) sq. cm
[Identify the given area]
Larger diagonal, \(d_1 = 72\) cm
[Identify the given larger diagonal]
Let the other diagonal be \(d_2\) cm
[Assume the unknown diagonal as d2]
Area of rhombus \\\(= \frac{1}{2} \times d_1 \times d_2\\\)
[Use the formula for the area of a rhombus]
\\\(1944 = \frac{1}{2} \times 72 \times d_2\\\)
[Substitute the known values]
\\\(1944 = 36 \times d_2\\\)
[Multiply 1/2 by 72]
\\\(d_2 = \frac{1944}{36} = 54\\\) cm
[Divide by 36 to find the second diagonal]
The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles.
[Note the property of rhombus diagonals]
Half-lengths of diagonals are \\\(\frac{72}{2} = 36\\\) cm and \\\(\frac{54}{2} = 27\\\) cm
[Find the length of the segments from the center to the vertices]
Length of each side of the rhombus, \\\(s = \sqrt{36^2 + 27^2}\\\)
[Apply Pythagoras' theorem to find the side length]
\\\(s = \sqrt{1296 + 729} = \sqrt{2025}\\\)
[Calculate the squares and add them]
\(s = 45\) cm
[Find the square root of 2025]
Perimeter of the rhombus \\\(= 4 \times s\\\)
[Use the formula for perimeter]
Perimeter \\\(= 4 \times 45 = 180\\\) cm [Ans.]
[Multiply the side by 4]

parts.text: Determine the perpendicular distance between two larger parallel sides.

parts.text: If mean of the lengths of two parallel sides of a trapezium is 11 and area is 121 square cm., then find the perpendicular distance between the parallel sides.
parts.answer:
Let the lengths of parallel sides of the trapezium be \(a\) and \(b\)
[Assume the lengths of the parallel sides]
Mean of the parallel sides \\\(= \frac{a + b}{2} = 11\\\)
[State the given mean value]
Area of the trapezium \\\(= \frac{a + b}{2} \times h = 121\\\) sq. cm
[Use the trapezium area formula]
\\\(11 \times h = 121\\\)

parts.text: Find the area of whole surface of the rectangular solid.
parts.answer:
Ratio of length, width, and height \(= 3 : 2 : 2\)
[State the given ratio]
Let length \(= 3x\), width \(= 2x\), and height \(= 2x\)
[Express dimensions in terms of a variable x]
Volume of rectangular solid \\\(= \text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{height}\\\)
[Use the volume formula]
\\\(768 = 3x \times 2x \times 2x\\\)
[Substitute the dimensions]
\(768 = 12x^3\)
[Multiply the terms]
\\\(x^3 = \frac{768}{12} = 64\\\)
[Divide by 12]
\\\(x = \sqrt[3]{64} = 4\\\) m
[Find the cube root of 64]
Dimensions are: length \\\(= 3 \times 4 = 12\\\) m, width \\\(= 2 \times 4 = 8\\\) m, height \\\(= 2 \times 4 = 8\\\) m

Total surface area \\\(= 2(\text{lw} + \text{wh} + \text{lh})\\\)
[Use the surface area formula]

[Sum the products and multiply by 2]

parts.text: If the length of a diagonal of the surface of a cube \\\(2\sqrt{2}\\\) cm, determine the area of its whole surface.

Given, \\\(a\sqrt{2} = 2\sqrt{2}\\\) cm
[Substitute the given value]
\(a = 2\) cm
[Divide both sides by \\\(\sqrt{2}\\\) to find the side length]
Total surface area of the cube \(= 6a^2\)
[Use the formula for the surface area of a cube]
\\\(\text{Area} = 6 \times 2^2 = 6 \times 4 = 24 \text{ sq. cm}\\\) [Ans.]

parts.text: Determine the area of the triangle.
parts.answer:
Let the length of the base of the isosceles triangle \(= b\)
[Assume base as b]
Length of equal sides \\\(= a = \frac{2}{3}b\\\)
[State the relationship given in the stem]
Perimeter \(= 2a + b = 6\) cm
[Use the formula for the perimeter of an isosceles triangle]
\\\(2(\frac{2}{3}b) + b = 6\\\)
[Substitute a in terms of b]
\\\(\frac{4}{3}b + b = 6 \Rightarrow \frac{7}{3}b = 6\\\)
[Combine the b terms]
\\\(b = \frac{6 \times 3}{7} = \frac{18}{7}\\\) cm
[Solve for b]
\\\(a = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{18}{7} = \frac{12}{7}\\\) cm
[Find the value of a]
Area of isosceles triangle \\\(= \frac{b}{4}\sqrt{4a^2 - b^2}\\\)
[Use the area formula for an isosceles triangle]
\\\(\text{Area} = \frac{18/7}{4}\sqrt{4(12/7)^2 - (18/7)^2}\\\)
[Substitute a and b]
\\\(\text{Area} = \frac{18}{28}\sqrt{\frac{576}{49} - \frac{324}{49}} = \frac{9}{14}\sqrt{\frac{252}{49}}\\\)
[Simplify the expression inside the root]
\\\(\text{Area} = \frac{9}{14} \times \frac{6\sqrt{7}}{7} = \frac{54\sqrt{7}}{98} = \frac{27\sqrt{7}}{49} \approx 1.46 \text{ sq. cm}\\\) [Ans.]
[Calculate the final decimal value]

[Use Heron's formula]

[Use basic triangle area formula where h is the height of the trapezium]

[Assume the side length is 'a']
Area of equilateral triangle \\\(= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2 \\\)
[Using the standard formula for the area of an equilateral triangle]
According to the question, \\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2 = 16\sqrt{3} \\\)
[Set the formula equal to the given area]
\\\(a^2 = \frac{16\sqrt{3} \times 4}{\sqrt{3}} \\\)
[Multiply both sides by 4 and divide by \\\(\sqrt{3}\\\) to isolate \( a^2 \)]

parts.text: If the perimeter of \\\(\Delta PQR\\\) is \\\(160 \text{ cm} \\\), and two of its sides are \\\(PQ = 50 \text{ cm} \\\) and \\\(QR = 60 \text{ cm} \\\), determine its area.
parts.answer:
Given, perimeter of \\\(\Delta PQR = 160 \text{ cm}\\\), \\\(PQ = 50 \text{ cm} \\\), and \\\(QR = 60 \text{ cm} \\\).
[Identify the given measurements]
Let the length of side \\\(PR = z \text{ cm} \\\).
[Define the unknown side as 'z']
\( 50 + 60 + z = 160 \)
[The sum of all sides equals the perimeter]
\( 110 + z = 160 \)
[Add the known sides]
\\\(z = 160 - 110 = 50 \text{ cm} \\\)
[Subtract 110 from both sides to find side PR]
Since \\\(PQ = PR = 50 \text{ cm} \\\), \\\(\Delta PQR\\\) is an isosceles triangle with base \\\(b = 60 \text{ cm} \\\) and equal sides \\\(a = 50 \text{ cm} \\\).
[Recognize that two sides are equal, making it an isosceles triangle]
Area of isosceles triangle \\\(= \frac{b}{4}\sqrt{4a^2 - b^2} \\\)
[Use the formula for the area of an isosceles triangle]
\\\(= \frac{60}{4}\sqrt{4(50)^2 - (60)^2} \\\)
[Substitute the values of a and b into the formula]
\\\(= 15\sqrt{4(2500) - 3600} \\\)
[Calculate the squares of 50 and 60]
\\\(= 15\sqrt{10000 - 3600} \\\)
[Multiply 4 by 2500]
\\\(= 15\sqrt{6400} \\\)
[Subtract 3600 from 10000]
\\\(= 15 \times 80 = 1200 \text{ sq. cm} \\\)
[Find the square root of 6400 and multiply by 15]
The area of \\\(\Delta PQR\\\) is \\\(1200 \text{ sq. cm} \\\). [Ans.]

parts.text: Determine the area of trapezium \( ABCD \) where parallel sides are \\\(AB = 84 \text{ cm} \\\) and \\\(CD = 54 \text{ cm} \\\), and other sides are \\\(AD = 12 \text{ cm} \\\) and \\\(BC = 18 \text{ cm} \\\).
parts.answer:
Given, parallel sides \\\(AB = 84 \text{ cm} \\\) and \\\(CD = 54 \text{ cm} \\\).
[Identify the bases of the trapezium]
Other sides are \\\(AD = 12 \text{ cm} \\\) and \\\(BC = 18 \text{ cm} \\\).
[Identify the non-parallel sides]
Sum of three sides \\\(AD, DC, \text{ and } BC = 12 + 54 + 18 \\\)
[Add the lengths of the three smaller sides]
\\\(= 84 \text{ cm} \\\)
[Result of the addition]
We observe that the sum of these three sides is equal to the length of the fourth side \\\(AB = 84 \text{ cm} \\\).
[Compare the sum to the remaining side]
In any quadrilateral, the sum of any three sides must be strictly greater than the fourth side to form a closed figure.
[Apply the geometric property of quadrilaterals]
Since \( 84 = 84 \), no trapezium can be formed, or the area of such a figure is zero.
[Conclude that the figure is degenerate]
The area of the trapezium is \( 0 \). [Ans.]

[Define the given variables]
Area of triangle \\\(= \frac{1}{2} \times a \times c \times \sin(\theta) \\\)
[Use the trigonometric formula for the area of a triangle]
\\\(= \frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 10 \times \sin(30^\circ) \\\)
[Substitute the values into the formula]
\\\(= \frac{1}{2} \times 90 \times \frac{1}{2} \\\)
[Substitute \\\(\sin(30^\circ) = 0.5\\\)]
\\\(= 22.5 \text{ sq. cm} \\\)
[Calculate the final product]
The area of the triangle is \\\(22.5 \text{ sq. cm} \\\). [Ans.]

parts.text: Determine the area of the whole surface of the rectangular solid.
parts.answer:
Let the length, breadth, and height of the solid be \( a = 12x \), \( b = 4x \), and \( c = 3x \).
[Express dimensions in terms of a common variable x based on the ratio]
The length of the diagonal is given as \\\(26 \text{ m} \\\).
[State the known diagonal length]
Diagonal \\\(= \sqrt{a^2 + b^2 + c^2} = 26 \\\)
[Use the formula for the diagonal of a rectangular solid]
\\\(\sqrt{(12x)^2 + (4x)^2 + (3x)^2} = 26 \\\)
[Substitute the expressions for a, b, and c]
\\\(\sqrt{144x^2 + 16x^2 + 9x^2} = 26 \\\)
[Square the terms inside the root]
\\\(\sqrt{169x^2} = 26 \\\)
[Sum the \( x^2 \) terms]
\( 13x = 26 \)
[Take the square root of both sides]
\( x = 2 \)
[Divide by 13 to find x]
Dimensions of the solid:
Length \\\(a = 12 \times 2 = 24 \text{ m} \\\)
Breadth \\\(b = 4 \times 2 = 8 \text{ m} \\\)
Height \\\(c = 3 \times 2 = 6 \text{ m} \\\)
[Calculate actual dimensions using \( x = 2 \)]
Whole surface area \( = 2(ab + bc + ca) \)
[Use the formula for the surface area of a rectangular solid]
\\\(= 2(24 \times 8 + 8 \times 6 + 6 \times 24) \\\)
[Substitute the calculated dimensions]
\( = 2(192 + 48 + 144) \)
[Multiply the pairs]
\\\(= 2(384) = 768 \text{ sq. m} \\\)
[Sum the values and multiply by 2]
The surface area of the solid is \\\(768 \text{ sq. m} \\\). [Ans.]

parts.text: If for planting grass the cost is Tk. 5 per square metre, determine the total cost for planting grass in the rhombus-shaped garden.
parts.answer:
Given, diagonal of the rhombus garden \\\(AC = \text{diagonal of solid} = 26 \text{ m} \\\).
[Link the garden's diagonal to the solid's diagonal from the stem]
Length of one side of the rhombus \\\(s = 15 \text{ m} \\\).
[State the given side length]
In a rhombus, diagonals bisect each other perpendicularly.
[State the geometric property of a rhombus]
Half of the first diagonal \\\(OA = \frac{26}{2} = 13 \text{ m} \\\).
[Divide the diagonal by 2 to find the distance from center to vertex]
Let the other diagonal be \( BD \). Half of it is \( OB \).
[Define the half-length of the second diagonal]
In right \\\(\Delta AOB\\\), by Pythagoras theorem:
\( OB^2 = AB^2 - OA^2 \)
[The side of the rhombus is the hypotenuse]
\( OB^2 = 15^2 - 13^2 \)
[Substitute the known values]
\( OB^2 = 225 - 169 = 56 \)
[Calculate the squares and subtract]
\\\(OB = \sqrt{56} = 2\sqrt{14} \approx 7.483 \text{ m} \\\)
[Take the square root]
Full diagonal \\\(BD = 2 \times OB = 2 \times 7.483 = 14.967 \text{ m} \\\)
[Multiply the half-length by 2]
Area of rhombus \\\(= \frac{1}{2} \times \text{Product of diagonals} \\\)
[Use the area formula for a rhombus]
\\\(= \frac{1}{2} \times 26 \times 14.967 = 194.571 \text{ sq. m} \\\)
[Calculate the area]
Total cost \\\(= \text{Area} \times \text{Rate} = 194.571 \times 5 \\\)
[Multiply area by the cost per square metre]
\\\(= 972.855 \approx 972.86 \text{ Taka} \\\)
[Final calculation]
The total cost for planting grass is \\\(972.86 \text{ Taka} \\\). [Ans.]

questions.questionText: The perimeter of the rectangular hallroom and the square shaped classroom is equal. The internal length of the hallroom is \( 1.5 \) times its width and the total cost of making the hallroom tiled is Tk. \( 45,000 \) by spending Tk. \( 75 \) per square meter. The two rooms are decorated with \\\(50 \text{ cm} \\\) square shaped tiles.

parts.text: Determine the area of the hallroom.
parts.answer:
Total cost of tiling \\\(= 45,000 \text{ Taka} \\\).
[State the given total cost]
Cost per square meter \\\(= 75 \text{ Taka} \\\).
[State the rate]
Area of the hallroom \\\(= \frac{\text{Total Cost}}{\text{Rate per sq. m}} \\\)
[Calculate area by dividing total cost by rate]
\\\(= \frac{45000}{75} = 600 \text{ square meter} \\\)
[Perform the division]
The area of the hallroom is \\\(600 \text{ sq. m} \\\). [Ans.]

parts.text: Determine the inner perimeter of the hallroom.
parts.answer:
Let the breadth of the hallroom be \\\(x \text{ meter} \\\).
[Define breadth as variable x]
Length \\\(= 1.5 \times x = \frac{3x}{2} \text{ meter} \\\).
[Length is 1.5 times the breadth]
Area of the hallroom \\\(= \text{Length} \times \text{Breadth} \\\)
[Use the area formula for a rectangle]
\\\(\frac{3x}{2} \times x = 600 \\\)
[Set the formula equal to the area found in part A]
\\\(\frac{3x^2}{2} = 600 \\\)
[Simplify the multiplication]
\( 3x^2 = 1200 \)
[Multiply both sides by 2]
\( x^2 = 400 \)
[Divide both sides by 3]
\\\(x = \sqrt{400} = 20 \text{ meter} \\\)
[Take the square root to find the breadth]
Breadth \\\(= 20 \text{ m} \\\).
Length \\\(= 1.5 \times 20 = 30 \text{ m} \\\).
[Calculate actual length using x]
Perimeter of the hallroom \\\(= 2(\text{Length} + \text{Breadth}) \\\)
[Use the perimeter formula for a rectangle]
\\\(= 2(30 + 20) = 2(50) = 100 \text{ meter} \\\)
[Sum length and breadth and multiply by 2]
The inner perimeter of the hallroom is \\\(100 \text{ m} \\\). [Ans.]

parts.text: How many tiles will be required to make these two rooms tiled? Determine.
parts.answer:
Perimeter of the square classroom \\\(= \text{Perimeter of the hallroom} = 100 \text{ meter} \\\).
[Use the information from the stem]
Side of the square classroom \\\(= \frac{\text{Perimeter}}{4} \\\)
[Divide perimeter by 4 to get the side of a square]
\\\(= \frac{100}{4} = 25 \text{ meter} \\\)
[Calculate side length]
Area of the square classroom \\\(= \text{side}^2 = (25)^2 = 625 \text{ square meter} \\\).
[Calculate area of square]
Total area of both rooms \\\(= \text{Hallroom area} + \text{Classroom area} \\\)
[Sum the areas of the two rooms]
\\\(= 600 + 625 = 1225 \text{ square meter} \\\).
[Perform addition]
Length of one side of a square tile \\\(= 50 \text{ cm} = 0.5 \text{ meter} \\\).
[Convert centimeters to meters]
Area of one square tile \\\(= (0.5)^2 = 0.25 \text{ square meter} \\\).
[Calculate the area of one tile]
Number of tiles required \\\(= \frac{\text{Total Area}}{\text{Area of one tile}} \\\)
[Divide total room area by tile area]
\\\(= \frac{1225}{0.25} = 4900 \\\)
[Perform the division]
The total number of tiles required is \( 4900 \). [Ans.]

questions.questionText: The volume of a cubic solid made with iron is \\\(343 \text{ cm}^3 \\\). Melting the solid a hollow cylindrical pipe is prepared. The inner and outer diameter of the hollow pipe are \\\(6 \text{ cm} \\\) and \\\(9 \text{ cm} \\\) respectively.

parts.text: If the area of a quadrilateral triangle is \\\(4\sqrt{3} \text{ sq. cm} \\\), then find its length of side.
parts.answer:
Let the side of the equilateral triangle be \\\(a \text{ cm} \\\).
[Define the side length as 'a']
Area of equilateral triangle \\\(= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2 \\\)
[Use the standard area formula]
According to the question, \\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2 = 4\sqrt{3} \\\)
[Set the formula equal to the given area]
\\\(a^2 = \frac{4\sqrt{3} \times 4}{\sqrt{3}} \\\)
[Isolate \( a^2 \)]
\( a^2 = 16 \)
[Simplify the calculation]
\\\(a = \sqrt{16} = 4 \text{ cm} \\\)
[Take the square root]
The length of the side is \\\(4 \text{ cm} \\\). [Ans.]

parts.text: Find the length of diagonal of a surface of the cubic solid.
parts.answer:
Let the edge of the cube be \\\(a \text{ cm} \\\).
[Define the edge length as 'a']
Volume of cube \\\(= a^3 = 343 \text{ cm}^3 \\\)
[Use the volume formula for a cube]
\\\(a = \sqrt[3]{343} = 7 \text{ cm} \\\)
[Take the cube root of 343]
Length of diagonal of a surface \\\(= \sqrt{a^2 + a^2} = a\sqrt{2} \\\)
[Use the formula for the diagonal of a square surface]
\\\(= 7\sqrt{2} \approx 9.899 \text{ cm} \\\)
[Substitute a and calculate the approximate value]
The length of the diagonal of a surface is \\\(9.899 \text{ cm} \\\). [Ans.]

parts.text: Find the height of the hollow pipe.
parts.answer:
Outer diameter \\\(= 9 \text{ cm} \implies \text{Outer radius } R = \frac{9}{2} = 4.5 \text{ cm} \\\).
[Calculate outer radius from diameter]
Inner diameter \\\(= 6 \text{ cm} \implies \text{Inner radius } r = \frac{6}{2} = 3 \text{ cm} \\\).
[Calculate inner radius from diameter]
Volume of hollow pipe \\\(= \pi(R^2 - r^2)h \\\)
[Use the formula for the volume of a hollow cylinder]
Given volume \\\(= 343 \text{ cm}^3 \\\) (since the cube was melted to make it).
[State that volume remains constant during melting]
\\\(343 = \pi(4.5^2 - 3^2)h \\\)
[Substitute the radii and volume]
\\\(343 = \pi(20.25 - 9)h \\\)
[Square the radii]
\\\(343 = 11.25\pi h \\\)
[Subtract the squares]
\\\(h = \frac{343}{11.25 \times 3.1416} \\\)
[Isolate h and substitute \\\(\pi \approx 3.1416\\\)]
\\\(h \approx \frac{343}{35.343} \approx 9.70 \text{ cm} \\\)
[Perform the final division]
The height of the hollow pipe is \\\(9.70 \text{ cm} \\\). [Ans.]

questions.questionText: The length of two adjacent sides of a parallelogram are \\\(20 \text{ cm} \\\) and \\\(15 \text{ cm} \\\) respectively and smaller diagonal is \\\(16 \text{ cm} \\\). Again, the outer diameter of an iron pipe is \\\(8 \text{ cm} \\\) and the inner diameter is \\\(6 \text{ cm} \\\) and the height of the pipe is \\\(10 \text{ meter} \\\). The weight of \\\(1 \text{ cm}^3 \\\) of iron pipe is \\\(7.2 \text{ gm} \\\).

parts.text: If the difference between the diameter and circumference of a circle is \\\(25 \text{ cm} \\\), find the radius of the circle.
parts.answer:
Let the radius of the circle be \\\(r \text{ cm} \\\).
[Define the radius as 'r']
Circumference \\\(= 2\pi r \\\) and Diameter \( = 2r \).
[State basic circle formulas]
According to the question, \\\(2\pi r - 2r = 25 \\\)
[Set up the equation based on the difference]
\\\(2r(\pi - 1) = 25 \\\)
[Factor out 2r]
\\\(r = \frac{25}{2(\pi - 1)} \\\)
[Isolate r]
\\\(r \approx \frac{25}{2(3.1416 - 1)} = \frac{25}{4.2832} \approx 5.84 \text{ cm} \\\)
[Substitute \\\(\pi\\\) and calculate]
The radius of the circle is \\\(5.84 \text{ cm} \\\). [Ans.]

parts.text: Determine the length of other diagonal of the parallelogram.
parts.answer:
Let the sides be \\\(AB = 15 \text{ m}, BC = 20 \text{ m} \\\) and smaller diagonal \\\(AC = 16 \text{ m} \\\).
[Assign given values to the parallelogram ABCD]
Semi-perimeter of \\\(\Delta ABC, s = \frac{15 + 20 + 16}{2} = 25.5 \text{ m} \\\).
[Calculate the semi-perimeter]
Area of \\\(\Delta ABC = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} \\\)
[Use Heron's formula for the area of the triangle]
\\\(= \sqrt{25.5(25.5-15)(25.5-20)(25.5-16)} \\\)
[Substitute the values]
\\\(= \sqrt{25.5 \times 10.5 \times 5.5 \times 9.5} \approx 118.279 \text{ sq. m} \\\).
[Calculate the product and take the square root]
Let \( AF \) be the altitude from \( A \) to base \( BC \).
Area of \\\(\Delta ABC = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} \\\)
\\\(118.279 = \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times AF \\\)
[Set the calculated area equal to the base-height formula]
\\\(10 AF = 118.279 \implies AF = 11.83 \text{ m} \\\).
[Solve for the altitude AF]
In right \\\(\Delta ABF\\\), \\\(BF = \sqrt{AB^2 - AF^2} = \sqrt{15^2 - 11.83^2} \\\)
[Use Pythagoras theorem to find the segment BF]
\\\(BF = \sqrt{225 - 139.95} = \sqrt{85.05} \approx 9.22 \text{ m} \\\).
[Calculate the square root]
In a parallelogram, let \( E \) be the extension of \( BC \). The other diagonal \( BD \) forms a right \\\(\Delta BDE\\\) where \( BE = BC + CE \).
Since \\\(CE = BF = 9.22 \text{ m} \\\),
\\\(BE = 20 + 9.22 = 29.22 \text{ m} \\\).
[Find the total base length for the larger triangle]
Using Pythagoras theorem in \\\(\Delta BDE\\\):
\\\(BD = \sqrt{BE^2 + DE^2} \\\) (where \\\(DE = AF = 11.83 \text{ m} \\\))
[The height DE is the same as altitude AF]
\\\(BD = \sqrt{(29.22)^2 + (11.83)^2} = \sqrt{853.8 + 139.9} = \sqrt{993.7} \approx 31.52 \text{ m} \\\).
[Calculate the final length of the diagonal]
The length of the other diagonal is \\\(31.52 \text{ m} \\\). [Ans.]

parts.text: Find the weight of the iron pipe.
parts.answer:
Outer radius \\\(R = \frac{8}{2} = 4 \text{ cm} \\\), Inner radius \\\(r = \frac{6}{2} = 3 \text{ cm} \\\).
[Calculate radii from diameters]
Height \\\(h = 10 \text{ m} = 1000 \text{ cm} \\\).
[Convert height from meters to centimeters to match other units]
Volume of iron \\\(= \pi(R^2 - r^2)h \\\)
[Use the volume formula for a hollow cylinder]
\\\(= \pi(4^2 - 3^2) \times 1000 \\\)
[Substitute the values]
\\\(= \pi(16 - 9) \times 1000 = 7000\pi \approx 21991.2 \text{ cm}^3 \\\).
[Calculate the volume]
Weight \\\(= \text{Volume} \times \text{Density} = 21991.2 \times 7.2 \\\)
[Multiply volume by the weight per cubic centimeter]
\\\(= 158336.64 \text{ g} \\\).
[Calculate weight in grams]
Converting to kilograms: \\\(\frac{158336.64}{1000} \approx 158.34 \text{ kg} \\\).
[Divide by 1000 to convert grams to kilograms]
The weight of the iron pipe is \\\(158.34 \text{ kg} \\\). [Ans.]

questions.questionText: Radius of a circle is \\\(5 \text{ cm} \\\). The volume of a right circular cylinder is \\\(150\pi \text{ cm}^3 \\\) and the radius of base of the cylinder is equal to the radius of the circle.

parts.text: If the perimeter of an equilateral triangle is \\\(12 \text{ cm} \\\), then find its area.
parts.answer:
Perimeter of equilateral triangle \\\(= 12 \text{ cm} \\\).
[State given perimeter]
Length of each side \\\(a = \frac{12}{3} = 4 \text{ cm} \\\).
[Divide by 3 for an equilateral triangle]
Area \\\(= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(4)^2 \\\)
[Use the area formula]
\\\(= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 16 = 4\sqrt{3} \text{ sq. cm} \\\).
[Simplify the multiplication]
The area of the triangle is \\\(4\sqrt{3} \text{ sq. cm} \\\). [Ans.]

parts.text: Find the area of curved surface of the cylinder.
parts.answer:
Radius of base of cylinder \\\(r = 5 \text{ cm} \\\).
[Radius is equal to the circle's radius from the stem]
Volume of cylinder \\\(V = \pi r^2 h = 150\pi \\\).
[Use the volume formula]
\\\(\pi(5)^2 h = 150\pi \implies 25\pi h = 150\pi \\\)
[Substitute radius and equate to given volume]
\\\(h = \frac{150\pi}{25\pi} = 6 \text{ cm} \\\).
[Solve for height h]
Curved Surface Area \\\(= 2\pi rh \\\)
[Use the formula for curved surface area of a cylinder]
\\\(= 2\pi(5)(6) = 60\pi \approx 188.5 \text{ sq. cm} \\\).
[Calculate final area]
The curved surface area of the cylinder is \\\(60\pi \text{ sq. cm} \\\). [Ans.]

parts.text: Find the difference between the area of above mentioned circle and the area of the square inscribed in that circle.
parts.answer:
Area of the circle \\\(= \pi r^2 = \pi(5)^2 = 25\pi \approx 78.54 \text{ sq. cm} \\\).
[Calculate circle area using \( r=5 \)]
For an inscribed square, the diagonal of the square equals the diameter of the circle.
Diagonal \\\(d = 2r = 2 \times 5 = 10 \text{ cm} \\\).
[Relate square diagonal to circle diameter]
Area of inscribed square \\\(= \frac{d^2}{2} = \frac{10^2}{2} = \frac{100}{2} = 50 \text{ sq. cm} \\\).
[Use the area formula for a square using its diagonal]
Difference in area \\\(= \text{Area of circle} - \text{Area of square} \\\)
[Subtract the square's area from the circle's area]
\\\(= 25\pi - 50 \approx 78.54 - 50 = 28.54 \text{ sq. cm} \\\).
[Calculate the final numerical difference]
The difference in area is \\\(28.54 \text{ sq. cm} \\\). [Ans.]

Area of the whole surface of the cube \(= 6a^2\)

According to the condition, \( 6a^2 = 1014 \)
[Set the surface area equal to the given value]

parts.text: Find the area of a rhombus whose two diagonals are \\\(20\text{ cm} \\\) and \\\(24\text{ cm} \\\).

parts.text: According to (i) find the area of the equilateral triangle.
parts.answer:
Let the length of each side of the equilateral triangle be \( a \) metres.
[Define variable for the side]
Area of the equilateral triangle \\\(= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2\text{ sq m} \\\).
[Formula for area of an equilateral triangle]
When the side is increased by \\\(10\text{ m} \\\), the new area \\\(= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (a + 10)^2\text{ sq m} \\\).
[Write area formula with the increased side]

[Difference in areas equals the given increase]
\\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \left( a^2 + 20a + 100 - a^2 \right) = 100\sqrt{3} \\\)

parts.text: If a wheel revolves 10 times to cover a distance of \\\(100\pi\text{ cm} \\\), determine its radius.
parts.answer:
Let the radius of the wheel be \( r \) cm.
[Define variable for radius]
Circumference of the wheel \\\(= 2\pi r\text{ cm} \\\).
[Formula for circumference]
Distance traversed by 10 rotations \\\(= 10 \times 2\pi r = 20\pi r\text{ cm} \\\).
[Distance = Number of rotations \\\(\times\\\) Circumference]
According to the question, \\\(20\pi r = 100\pi \\\)
[Set the calculated distance equal to the given distance]
\\\(r = \frac{100\pi}{20\pi} = 5\text{ cm} \\\)
[Divide to isolate \( r \)]
Result: \\\(5\text{ cm} \\\) [Ans.]

parts.text: Find the length of smaller diagonal of the rhombus.
parts.answer:
Perimeter of the rhombus ABCD \\\(= 180\text{ cm} \\\).
[Identify given perimeter]
Length of each side \\\(= \frac{180}{4} = 45\text{ cm} \\\).
[A rhombus has 4 equal sides]
Let the diagonals be \( d_1 \) and \( d_2 \). Given \\\(d_1 = 72\text{ cm} \\\).
[Identify given diagonal]
The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles.
[Geometric property of rhombus]
Half of the greater diagonal \\\(= \frac{72}{2} = 36\text{ cm} \\\).
[Calculate half length]
Let half of the smaller diagonal be \( x \).
[Define variable for half of second diagonal]
Using Pythagoras theorem in \\\(\Delta AOB\\\):
\( x^2 + 36^2 = 45^2 \)
[Sum of squares of legs equals square of hypotenuse]
\( x^2 = 45^2 - 36^2 \)
[Isolate \( x^2 \)]
\( x^2 = 2025 - 1296 = 729 \)
[Calculate squares and subtract]
\\\(x = \sqrt{729} = 27\text{ cm} \\\)
[Take square root]
Length of the smaller diagonal \\\(d_2 = 2 \times 27 = 54\text{ cm} \\\).
[Double the half length to get full diagonal]
Result: \\\(54\text{ cm} \\\) [Ans.]

parts.text: Find the perimeter of the equilateral triangle.
parts.answer:
Let the length of each side of the equilateral triangle be \( a \) metres.
[Define variable for side]
Area of the triangle \\\(= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2\text{ sq m} \\\).
[Formula for area]
When the side increases by \\\(1\text{ m} \\\), new area \\\(= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (a + 1)^2\text{ sq m} \\\).
[Write area with increased side]
According to the question:
\\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (a + 1)^2 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = 4\sqrt{3} \\\)
[Difference in areas equals the given increase]
\\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (a^2 + 2a + 1 - a^2) = 4\sqrt{3} \\\)
[Expand square and simplify]
\\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (2a + 1) = 4\sqrt{3} \\\)
[Further simplify]
\\\(2a + 1 = 4 \times 4 \\\)
[Divide both sides by \\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\\\)]
\( 2a + 1 = 16 \)
[Simplify multiplication]
\( 2a = 15 \)
[Subtract 1 from both sides]
\\\(a = 7.5\text{ m} \\\)
[Divide by 2]
Perimeter of the equilateral triangle \\\(= 3a = 3 \times 7.5 = 22.5\text{ m} \\\).
[Perimeter is 3 times the side length]
Result: \\\(22.5\text{ m} \\\) [Ans.]

parts.text: The radius of a circle is \\\(6\text{ metre} \\\) and an arc subtends an angle \\\(60^\circ \\\) at its centre. Determine the area of the circular segment.
parts.answer:
Given, radius \\\(r = 6\text{ m} \\\) and angle \\\(\theta = 60^\circ \\\).
[Identify given values]
Area of the sector \\\(= \frac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^2 = \frac{60}{360} \times 3.1416 \times 6^2\\\)
[Formula for sector area]
\\\(= \frac{1}{6} \times 3.1416 \times 36 = 6 \times 3.1416 \approx 18.85\text{ sq m} \\\).
[Simplify and calculate]
Area of the triangle formed by the arc \\\(= \frac{1}{2} r^2 \sin \theta = \frac{1}{2} \times 6^2 \times \sin(60^\circ)\\\)
[Formula for area of triangle within sector]
\\\(= \frac{1}{2} \times 36 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 9\sqrt{3} \approx 15.59\text{ sq m} \\\).
[Calculate using \\\(\sin 60^\circ = \sqrt{3}/2 \\\)]
Area of the circular segment \\\(= \text{Area of sector} - \text{Area of triangle}\\\)
[Segment area is sector minus triangle]
\\\(= 18.85 - 15.59 = 3.26\text{ sq m} \\\).
[Subtract the values]
Result: \\\(3.26\text{ sq m} \\\) [Ans.]

\\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (a + 4)^2 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 = 20\sqrt{3} \\\)
[Difference in areas equals the given increase]
\\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (a^2 + 8a + 16 - a^2) = 20\sqrt{3} \\\)
[Expand square and simplify]
\\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (8a + 16) = 20\sqrt{3} \\\)
[Further simplify]
\\\(8a + 16 = 20 \times 4 \\\)
[Divide both sides by \\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\\\)]
\( 8a + 16 = 80 \)
[Simplify multiplication]
\\\(8a = 64 \implies a = 8\text{ m} \\\)
[Isolate \( a \)]
Area of the triangle \\\(= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (8)^2 = \frac{64\sqrt{3}}{4} = 16\sqrt{3}\text{ sq m} \\\).

Result: Side \\\(= 8\text{ m} \\\), Area \\\(= 16\sqrt{3}\text{ sq m} \\\) [Ans.]

[Calculate squares]

Result: \\\(20\sqrt{2}\text{ m} \\\) [Ans.]

parts.text: If the difference between the diameter and circumference of a circle is \( 66 \) cm. Find the radius of the circle.
parts.answer:
Let the radius of the circle be \( r \) cm.
[Assign a variable to the unknown radius]
According to the question:
\\\(2\pi r - 2r = 66 \\\)
[Subtract the diameter from the circumference as stated in the problem]
\\\(2r(\pi - 1) = 66 \\\)
[Factor out \( 2r \) from the left side]
\\\(r = \frac{66}{2(\pi - 1)} \\\)
[Isolate \( r \) by dividing both sides by \\\(2(\pi - 1) \\\)]
\\\(r = \frac{33}{\pi - 1} \\\)
[Simplify the fraction]
\\\(r \approx 15.41 \\\) cm [Ans.]
[Calculate the numerical value using \\\(\pi \approx 3.14159 \\\)]

parts.text: How many stones will be required to cover the square region with square stone of \( 50 \) cm each and each stone costs Tk. \( 25 \). How much money will be needed to cover the square?
parts.answer:
Let the breadth of the rectangle be \( x \) metres.
[Assign a variable to the breadth]
Then the length is \( 3x \) metres.
[Length is thrice the breadth]
Area of the rectangle = \\\(\text{length} \times \text{breadth} = 3x \times x = 3x^2 \\\) sq. metres.
[Use the area formula for a rectangle]
According to the question:
\( 3x^2 = 1200 \)
[Equate calculated area to the given area]
\\\(x^2 = \frac{1200}{3} = 400 \\\)
[Divide both sides by 3]
\\\(x = \sqrt{400} = 20 \\\) metres
[Take the square root of both sides to find the breadth]
So, breadth = \( 20 \) m and length = \\\(3 \times 20 = 60 \\\) m.
[Calculate the specific dimensions]
Perimeter of the rectangle = \\\(2(\text{length} + \text{breadth}) = 2(60 + 20) = 160 \\\) metres.
[Calculate the total perimeter of the rectangle]
Since the perimeter of the square region is equal to the perimeter of the rectangle:
Perimeter of square = \( 160 \) metres.
[Equate the two perimeters]
Let the side of the square be \( a \). Then, \( 4a = 160 \).
[Set up the perimeter formula for a square]
\\\(a = \frac{160}{4} = 40 \\\) metres.
[Divide by 4 to find the length of one side]
Area of the square region = \( 40^2 = 1600 \) sq. metres.
[Calculate the area of the square]
Side of square stone = \( 50 \) cm = \( 0.5 \) metres.
[Convert centimeters to meters for consistency]
Area of one square stone = \( 0.5^2 = 0.25 \) sq. metres.
[Calculate the area of a single stone]
Number of stones required = \\\(\frac{1600}{0.25} = 6400 \\\).
[Divide the total area by the area of one stone]
Total cost = \\\(6400 \times 25 = 1,60,000 \\\) Tk. [Ans.]
[Multiply the number of stones by the price per stone]

parts.text: If the length of greater diagonal is \( 32 \) cm, find its other diagonal and the area?
parts.answer:
Given, perimeter of the rhombus = \( 80 \) cm.
[Identify given information]
Length of one side of the rhombus = \\\(\frac{80}{4} = 20 \\\) cm.
[A rhombus has four equal sides]
Let the diagonals be \( d_1 \) and \( d_2 \). Given \( d_1 = 32 \) cm.
[Identify the length of the greater diagonal]
In a rhombus, diagonals bisect each other at right angles.
[State geometric property of rhombus diagonals]
Half of greater diagonal = \\\(\frac{32}{2} = 16 \\\) cm.
[Find half the length of the given diagonal]
Let the half of the smaller diagonal be \( x \).
By Pythagoras theorem:
\( x^2 + 16^2 = 20^2 \)
[Sum of squares of half-diagonals equals the square of the side]
\( x^2 + 256 = 400 \)
[Calculate the squares of the numbers]
\( x^2 = 400 - 256 = 144 \)
[Subtract 256 from both sides]
\\\(x = \sqrt{144} = 12 \\\) cm.
[Find the value of \( x \)]
Length of smaller diagonal = \\\(2 \times 12 = 24 \\\) cm. [Ans.]
[Double the half-diagonal to get the full length]
Area of the rhombus = \\\(\frac{1}{2} \times \text{diagonal}_1 \times \text{diagonal}_2 \\\)
[Use the area formula for a rhombus]
Area = \\\(\frac{1}{2} \times 32 \times 24 = 384 \\\) sq. cm. [Ans.]
[Multiply and divide to find the final area]

parts.text: The length of the two sides of a triangle are \( 10 \) cm and \( 12 \) cm respectively and the angle included them is \\\(30^\circ \\\). Find the area of the triangle.
parts.answer:
Given, sides \( a = 10 \) cm, \( b = 12 \) cm, and included angle \\\(\theta = 30^\circ \\\).
[Identify given measurements]
Area of triangle = \\\(\frac{1}{2} ab \sin(\theta) \\\)
[Use the trigonometric formula for area of a triangle]
Area = \\\(\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 12 \times \sin(30^\circ) \\\)
[Substitute the known values]
Area = \\\(60 \times \frac{1}{2} = 30 \\\) sq. cm. [Ans.]
[Calculate the final area using \\\(\sin(30^\circ) = 0.5 \\\)]

parts.text: How many stones will be required to cover the square region with square shaped stones of \( 40 \) cm each?
parts.answer:
Let the breadth of the rectangle be \( x \) metres.
[Assign a variable to the breadth]
Then the length is \( 5x \) metres.
[Length is five times the breadth]
Area of rectangle = \\\(\text{length} \times \text{breadth} = 5x \times x = 5x^2 \\\) sq. metres.
[Use the area formula]
According to the question:
\( 5x^2 = 1280 \)
[Equate to the given area]
\\\(x^2 = \frac{1280}{5} = 256 \\\)
[Divide both sides by 5]
\\\(x = \sqrt{256} = 16 \\\) metres.
[Find the square root of 256]
So, breadth = \( 16 \) m and length = \\\(5 \times 16 = 80 \\\) m.
[Determine the actual dimensions]
Perimeter of the rectangle = \( 2(80 + 16) = 2(96) = 192 \) metres.
[Calculate the rectangle's perimeter]
Perimeter of square = \( 192 \) metres.
[Equate perimeters as per the stem]
Let the side of the square be \( a \). Then \( 4a = 192 \).
[Set up the perimeter formula for a square]
\\\(a = \frac{192}{4} = 48 \\\) metres.
[Find the side length]
Area of the square region = \( 48^2 = 2304 \) sq. metres.
[Calculate the total area to be covered]
Side of square stone = \( 40 \) cm = \( 0.4 \) metres.
[Convert cm to m]
Area of one square stone = \( 0.4^2 = 0.16 \) sq. metres.
[Calculate the area of one stone]
Number of stones required = \\\(\frac{2304}{0.16} = 14400 \\\). [Ans.]
[Divide the total area by the area of one stone]

parts.text: If the smaller diagonal of the parallelogram is \( 56 \) cm, then find the length of the other diagonal.
parts.answer:
Let the parallelogram be \( ABCD \). Sides are \( BC = 60 \) cm and \( AB = 52 \) cm.
[Identify dimensions]
Smaller diagonal \( AC = 56 \) cm.
[Identify the given diagonal]
In \\\(\triangle ABC\\\), semi-perimeter \\\(s = \frac{60 + 52 + 56}{2} = \frac{168}{2} = 84 \\\) cm.
[Calculate semi-perimeter for Heron's formula]
Area of \\\(\triangle ABC = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}\\\)
[Use Heron's formula for the area of the triangle]
Area = \\\(\sqrt{84(84-60)(84-52)(84-56)} = \sqrt{84 \times 24 \times 32 \times 28} = 1344 \\\) sq. cm.
[Calculate the area of half the parallelogram]
Let the height of the parallelogram (from \( A \) to \( BC \)) be \( h \).
Area of \\\(\triangle ABC = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 60 \times h = 1344 \\\).
[Relate triangle area to base and height]
\\\(30h = 1344 \Rightarrow h = \frac{1344}{30} = 44.8 \\\) cm.
[Solve for height \( h \)]
Let \( E \) be the foot of the perpendicular from \( A \) to the line containing \( BC \).
In right \\\(\triangle ABE\\\), \( BE^2 = AB^2 - AE^2 = 52^2 - 44.8^2 \).
[Use Pythagoras theorem to find the projection of the side on the base]
\( BE^2 = 2704 - 2007.04 = 696.96 \)
[Calculate the squares]
\\\(BE = \sqrt{696.96} = 26.4 \\\) cm.
[Find the length of \( BE \)]
Since \( E \) is outside the segment \( BC \), the distance \( BF = BC + CF = 60 + 26.4 = 86.4 \) cm.
[Calculate the base for the second triangle formed by the other diagonal]
Let the other diagonal be \( BD \).
In right \\\(\triangle BDF\\\), \( BD^2 = BF^2 + DF^2 \) (where \( DF = AE = 44.8 \)).
[Use Pythagoras theorem for the other diagonal]
\( BD^2 = 86.4^2 + 44.8^2 = 7464.96 + 2007.04 = 9472 \).
[Calculate the squares and sum them]
\\\(BD = \sqrt{9472} \approx 97.32 \\\) cm. [Ans.]
[Find the final length of the other diagonal]

questions.questionText: (i) The inner and outer diameter of an iron pipe is \( 16 \) cm and \( 18 \) cm respectively. The height of the pipe is \( 7 \) meter. The weight of \\\(1 \text{ cm}^3 \\\) iron is \( 7.2 \) gm. (ii) Length of three sides of a triangle are \( 7 \) cm, \( 8 \) cm, \( 9 \) cm respectively.

parts.text: Determine the area of the curved surface of inner side of the pipe.
parts.answer:
Inner diameter = \( 16 \) cm.
[Identify given diameter]
Inner radius \\\(r = \frac{16}{2} = 8 \\\) cm.
[Calculate radius as half of diameter]
Height of pipe \\\(h = 7 \text{ m} = 700 \\\) cm.
[Convert meters to centimeters]
Area of the curved surface = \\\(2\pi rh \\\)
[Use the curved surface area formula for a cylinder]
Area = \\\(2 \times 3.1416 \times 8 \times 700 \approx 35185.84 \\\) sq. cm. [Ans.]
[Substitute values and calculate the final area]

parts.text: Find the weight of the iron of pipe in kg.
parts.answer:
Outer diameter = \( 18 \) cm, so Outer radius \( R = 9 \) cm.
[Calculate outer radius]
Outer volume of the pipe = \\\(\pi R^2 h = 3.1416 \times 9^2 \times 700 \approx 178128.72 \\\) cubic cm.
[Calculate the volume based on outer radius]
Inner volume of the pipe = \\\(\pi r^2 h = 3.1416 \times 8^2 \times 700 \approx 140743.68 \\\) cubic cm.
[Calculate the volume based on inner radius]
Volume of iron used = \( 178128.72 - 140743.68 = 37385.04 \) cubic cm.
[Subtract inner volume from outer volume to find material volume]
Weight of iron = \\\(37385.04 \times 7.2 = 269172.288 \\\) gm.
[Multiply volume by density]
Weight in kg = \\\(\frac{269172.288}{1000} \approx 269.17 \\\) kg. [Ans.]
[Convert grams to kilograms]

parts.text: Determine the perimeter of an equilateral triangle whose area is equal to the area of the triangle mentioned in (ii).
parts.answer:
Sides of the triangle are \( 7, 8, 9 \) cm.
[Identify given side lengths]
Semi-perimeter \\\(s = \frac{7 + 8 + 9}{2} = 12 \\\) cm.
[Calculate semi-perimeter]
Area of triangle = \\\(\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} = \sqrt{12(12-7)(12-8)(12-9)} \\\)
[Use Heron's formula]
Area = \\\(\sqrt{12 \times 5 \times 4 \times 3} = \sqrt{720} \approx 26.83 \\\) sq. cm.
[Calculate numerical area]
Area of an equilateral triangle with side \( x \) = \\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} x^2 \\\).
[Use the equilateral triangle area formula]
According to the question:
\\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} x^2 = 26.83 \\\)
[Equate the two areas]
\\\(x^2 = \frac{26.83 \times 4}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 61.96 \\\)
[Isolate \( x^2 \)]
\\\(x = \sqrt{61.96} \approx 7.87 \\\) cm.
[Find the side length]
Perimeter of equilateral triangle = \\\(3 \times 7.87 = 23.61 \\\) cm. [Ans.]
[Multiply the side by 3 to find the total perimeter]

parts.text: If the area of the whole surface of a cube is \( 108 \) square meter, then find the length of diagonal.
parts.answer:
Let the side of the cube be \( a \) metres.
[Define side variable]
Total surface area of a cube = \( 6a^2 \).
[Use the surface area formula for a cube]
According to the question:
\( 6a^2 = 108 \)
[Equate to given surface area]
\\\(a^2 = \frac{108}{6} = 18 \\\)
[Divide by 6]
\\\(a = \sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2} \\\) metres.
[Simplify the square root]
Length of diagonal of a cube = \\\(a\sqrt{3} = 3\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{3} = 3\sqrt{6} \\\) metres. [Ans.]
[Use the diagonal formula for a cube]

parts.text: If the length of the diagonal of a square is \\\(30\sqrt{2} \\\) cm, then find the area of an equilateral triangle.
parts.answer:
Let the side of the square be \( x \) cm.
[Define side variable]
Diagonal of the square = \\\(x\sqrt{2} \\\).
[Use the diagonal formula for a square]
According to the question:
\\\(x\sqrt{2} = 30\sqrt{2} \\\)
[Equate to the given diagonal]
\( x = 30 \) cm.
[Divide both sides by \\\(\sqrt{2} \\\)]
Perimeter of the square = \\\(4 \times 30 = 120 \\\) cm.

Perimeter of equilateral triangle = \( 120 \) cm.
[Equate perimeters]
Side of equilateral triangle = \\\(\frac{120}{3} = 40 \\\) cm.

Area of equilateral triangle = \\\(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 40^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 1600 = 400\sqrt{3} \approx 692.82 \\\) sq. cm. [Ans.]
[Substitute into the area formula and calculate]

parts.text: Determine the area of its whole surface of the solid that is formed by revolving the rectangle around its greater side.

The rectangle is revolved around its greater side (\( 8 \) m).

This forms a cylinder where height \( h = 8 \) m and radius \( r = 6 \) m.

Total surface area of cylinder = \\\(2\pi r(r + h) \\\)
[Use the total surface area formula for a cylinder]
Total surface area = \\\(2 \times 3.1416 \times 6(6 + 8) \\\)
[Substitute values]
Total surface area = \\\(37.6992 \times 14 \approx 527.79 \\\) sq. metres. [Ans.]
[Perform final calculation]

parts.text: If the length of each side of a regular pentagon is \\\(6 \text{ cm} \\\), find its area.
parts.answer:
Let the side of the regular pentagon be \\\(a = 6 \text{ cm} \\\) and number of sides \( n = 5 \).
[Define the given values for the pentagon]
Area of a regular polygon \\\(= \frac{na^2}{4} \cot\left(\frac{180^\circ}{n}\right) \text{ sq. cm} \\\)
[Apply the standard formula for the area of a regular polygon]
\\\(= \frac{5 \times 6^2}{4} \cot\left(\frac{180^\circ}{5}\right) \\\)
[Substitute \( n = 5 \) and \( a = 6 \)]
\\\(= 45 \times \cot(36^\circ) \\\)
[Simplify the fraction and the angle]
\\\(= 45 \times 1.376 \\\)
[Use a calculator to find the value of \\\(\cot(36^\circ) \\\)]
\\\(= 61.92 \text{ sq. cm} \\\)
[Final multiplication]
Result: \\\(61.92 \text{ sq. cm (approx)} \\\) [Ans.]

parts.text: The area of PQRS parallelogram is equal to the area of a square region. Find the length of the diagonal of the square.
parts.answer:
From the figure, base of the parallelogram \( QR = 45 \) and height \( PT = 5 \).
[Identify the dimensions of the parallelogram from the diagram]
Area of parallelogram PQRS \\\(= \text{base} \times \text{height} \\\)
[Apply the area formula for a parallelogram]
\\\(= 45 \times 5 = 225 \text{ sq. units} \\\)
[Calculate the area]
According to the question, Area of square region \\\(= 225 \text{ sq. units} \\\)
[Equate the square's area to the parallelogram's area]
Let the side of the square be \( a \).
\( a^2 = 225 \)
[The area of a square is side squared]
\\\(a = \sqrt{225} = 15 \text{ units} \\\)
[Take the square root to find the side length]
Diagonal of the square \\\(= a\sqrt{2} \\\)
[Apply the diagonal formula for a square]
\\\(= 15\sqrt{2} \approx 21.21 \text{ units} \\\)
[Calculate the final numerical value]
Result: \\\(21.21 \text{ units (approx)} \\\) [Ans.]

parts.text: Find the area of the quadrilateral ABCD.
parts.answer:
Since \\\(AD \parallel BC \\\) and the non-parallel sides are unequal, ABCD is a trapezium.
[Identify the shape based on given properties]
Let the perpendicular height be \( h \), and distance \( BF = x \).
[Assign variables to the unknown height and segment]
In right triangle \\\(\triangle ABF\\\):
\( AB^2 = AF^2 + BF^2 \)
[Apply the Pythagorean theorem]
\\\(10^2 = h^2 + x^2 \Rightarrow h^2 = 100 - x^2 \dots (i) \\\)
[Substitute values and express \( h^2 \) in terms of \( x \)]
In right triangle \\\(\triangle CDG\\\), the base segment \( CG = BC - (BF + FG) \).
Since \( FG = AD = 7 \), \( CG = 12 - (x + 7) = 5 - x \).
[Calculate the length of the base segment \( CG \)]
\( CD^2 = CG^2 + DG^2 \)
[Apply the Pythagorean theorem for the second triangle]
\( 8^2 = (5 - x)^2 + h^2 \)
[Substitute known values]
\( 64 = (25 - 10x + x^2) + (100 - x^2) \)
[Substitute \( h^2 \) from equation (i)]
\( 64 = 125 - 10x \)
[Simplify the equation by canceling \( x^2 \)]
\( 10x = 125 - 64 = 61 \)
[Isolate the term with \( x \)]
\\\(x = 6.1 \text{ cm} \\\)
[Find the value of \( x \)]
Substitute \( x = 6.1 \) into \( h^2 = 100 - x^2 \):
\( h^2 = 100 - (6.1)^2 = 100 - 37.21 = 62.79 \)
[Calculate the value of \( h^2 \)]
\\\(h = \sqrt{62.79} \approx 7.92 \text{ cm} \\\)
[Find the height \( h \)]
Area of trapezium ABCD \\\(= \frac{1}{2} \times (AD + BC) \times h \\\)
[Apply the area formula for a trapezium]
\\\(= \frac{1}{2} \times (7 + 12) \times 7.92 \\\)
[Substitute the lengths and height]
\\\(= \frac{1}{2} \times 19 \times 7.92 = 75.24 \text{ sq. cm} \\\)
[Perform the final calculation]
Result: \\\(75.24 \text{ sq. cm (approx)} \\\) [Ans.]

parts.text: Find the area of an equilateral triangle if the length of one side is \\\(\sqrt{3} \text{ cm} \\\).
parts.answer:
Let the side of the equilateral triangle be \\\(a = \sqrt{3} \text{ cm} \\\).
[Identify the given side length]
Area of equilateral triangle \\\(= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2 \\\)
[Apply the specific area formula for an equilateral triangle]
\\\(= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times (\sqrt{3})^2 \\\)
[Substitute the value of \( a \)]
\\\(= \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4} \approx 1.299 \text{ sq. cm} \\\)
[Calculate the final numerical result]
Result: \\\(1.299 \text{ sq. cm (approx)} \\\) [Ans.]

parts.text: Determine the length of the arc LN and the area of the circular segment LMN.
parts.answer:
Given, radius \\\(r = 14 \text{ cm} \\\) and angle \\\(\theta = 30^\circ \\\).
[Identify the given dimensions for the circular sector]
Length of arc LN \\\(= \frac{\pi r \theta}{180^\circ} \\\)
[Apply the arc length formula]
\\\(= \frac{3.1416 \times 14 \times 30}{180} \approx 7.33 \text{ cm} \\\)
[Substitute values and solve]
Area of circular segment LMN \\\(= \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times \pi r^2 \\\)
[Apply the area formula for a circular sector/segment]
\\\(= \frac{30}{360} \times 3.1416 \times 14^2 \\\)
[Substitute values]
\\\(= \frac{1}{12} \times 3.1416 \times 196 \approx 51.31 \text{ sq. cm} \\\)
[Perform the final multiplication]
Result: Arc length \\\(7.33 \text{ cm} \\\), Area \\\(51.31 \text{ sq. cm} \\\) [Ans.]

parts.text: Find the area of the whole surface and the volume of the above figure (cylinder).
parts.answer:
Given, height \\\(h = 30 \text{ cm} \\\) and radius \\\(r = 14 \text{ cm} \\\).
[Identify the cylinder's dimensions]
Total surface area \\\(= 2\pi r(r + h) \\\)
[Apply the total surface area formula for a cylinder]
\\\(= 2 \times 3.1416 \times 14 \times (14 + 30) \\\)
[Substitute the values]
\\\(= 2 \times 3.1416 \times 14 \times 44 \approx 3870.45 \text{ sq. cm} \\\)
[Calculate the result]
Volume of the cylinder \\\(= \pi r^2 h \\\)
[Apply the volume formula for a cylinder]
\\\(= 3.1416 \times 14^2 \times 30 \\\)
[Substitute the values]
\\\(= 3.1416 \times 196 \times 30 \approx 18472.61 \text{ cubic cm} \\\)
[Perform final multiplication]
Result: Surface Area \\\(3870.45 \text{ sq. cm} \\\), Volume \\\(18472.61 \text{ cubic cm} \\\) [Ans.]
